payload.title: Shared Memory Swizzling and Bank Conflict Elimination
payload.summary: NVIDIA GPU's Shared Memory (SMEM) achieves high bandwidth through **parallel bank access**, but when multiple threads access the same bank simultaneously, **bank conflicts** occur, leading to serialization. This article explains the SMEM banking model, common conflict scenarios, and the principles and practices of using XOR swizzle to eliminate conflicts.

sections.heading: Overview
sections.gist: NVIDIA GPU's Shared Memory (SMEM) achieves high bandwidth through **parallel bank access**, but when multiple threads access the same bank simultaneously, **bank conflicts** occur, leading to serialization.

sections.heading: 2. Common Bank Conflict Scenarios
sections.gist: This is the most classic source of bank conflicts.

sections.heading: 3. Solution 1: Padding
sections.gist: The simplest method: add padding at the end of each row to break bank alignment.

sections.heading: 4. Solution 2: XOR Swizzle (Key Focus)
sections.gist: Swizzle uses **bitwise operations (XOR)** to remap SMEM addresses, distributing originally conflicting access patterns across different banks while preserving data locality and vectorization capability.
